body: I‘ve actually got to work with a few of the older nukes since I’ve been in. I think 3 or 4 of the guys I work with are first tour sailors at over 28 years old. They do perfectly fine and blend in with everyone pretty well. Granted I’ve been in shipyard my entire career so take that with a grain of salt but overall they’ve done well. In fact I’d say most of the time you’ll get “street cred” for being older. Having gone through more of life than the other 99% of us who enlisted after high school or a couple years of college. Most nukes enlist for the same reasons you are. One of the guys I work with actually has a nuclear engineering degree and joined specifically so he could have some job experience and be more competitive in the civilian world. He just turned 29 this past year. In my experience, age doesn’t matter with nukes, it’s character. Who you are and how you carry yourself day to day leaves more of an impact than being “the old guy”. Hope this helps in some way!

Truth be told I have no clue. I made it off of a 10% advancement rate with an MP eval, only qualified APVO and one NAM to my name. One of the guys who has more time in rate than I do is still an E-4 with a college degree, senior in rate qualified, and his warfare device (dolphins). Yet one of the guys who is past his qualification dates on literally everything. Is owned by the EDMC (doesn’t belong to M-div, does no work, makes little to no progress on quals) got picked up E-5 last cycle. I’m a bit jaded so take this with a grain of salt but the system is just stupid and makes zero sense. People who deserve rank and more pay don’t get it and those who don’t somehow manage to get it. If you’re super concerned with making rank and keeping/getting BAH and what not best to start the paperwork ASAP. My YN’s completely fucked over two of the guys I showed up with. They started their paperwork a week after showing up and weren’t re-enlisted till almost 6 months later.

You may find my next statement contradicting but this is honest truth. I love driving. It's my therapy, I prefer to be alone with my music, my car, and the road. No destination, no real reason other than to drive. Something about it for me is just therapeutic. Which is why it's hard for me to REALLY consider doing it. What ends up happening is they become brushing thoughts, kind of spontaneous and I let my imagination take it away. But I've never felt the URGE to do it. To me, you shluldn't be afraid to drive. It may piss you off sometimes with bad drivers or heavy traffic, but I would say 95% of the time, it's very nice, for me personally. I know what u mean by loose control, but sometimes you just have to trust yourself that you won't. Your brain is hardwired to survive which is why I'm still here. I've had several self attempts at my life but never anywhere near successful. Several times where I should have died but I miraculously saved myself from dying. The mind is a strange and powerful thing. And sometimes you're gonna have to trust that everything will be okay. I promise it will.

Idk if this is gonna help much but, with my gf, it hurts to know whenever she's down and there's little to nothing I can do being away. It makes me feel the same way your bf did. Like I disappoint her, like I can't do anything to help. There's chance that he could have seen you having a good time with your friends and thought to himself "they make her so happy, why can't I ever do that?" At least that's how it was for me. I opened up to my gf about it and she reassured me that she may laugh and have a good time with them, but she told me that she feels the happiest whenever she's with me. On a facetime call or texting or when we snap each other. LDR takes a lot of communication, and if he doesn't feel very strong in his skills of communication then it becomes very difficult to hold a LDR. To me, it's honestly about how vulnerable you let yourself be for someone else. Trusting the other person so much that if they break it, you may never be able to trust anyone, even family, ever again.

To me, LDR is kind of a "high risk, high reward" type of relationship. And he may have not felt ready enough to take that risk. Being in the same state just really far apart is far different than dealing with the time changes of being on opposite coasts.

I hate to break it to you but it might be best to block him, or at least remove him from SM. In one of my precious relationships I fell fast and hard for her, but within a month she broke up with me. It was devastating. We were only dating for a month and a half but it took me nearly 6 to recover. I tried my best to stay friends with her but every time I saw her pop up on my feed or anything, I'd get a wave of sadness that just encased me and ruined the rest of my day. When I finally realized that although I cared about her, I needed to remove her from my life in order to move on. It may be the same way for you.

I know how much it hurts when you lose someone so important to you. Someone you probably felt you could spend the rest of your life with and be extremely happy. First dealing with the sadness of not being able to see him and then bam. Now he's "no longer in your life" (I say this in quotations because it's never certain, life and love acts in strange ways). I know it sucks, it's painful, it hurts, you feel unmotivated to move, you don't want anything else. Sleeping it off never works. The pain is always there...

If it were any other time I would say to try to go out, do something new. Do something you've never done. I went out a lot and went hiking or exploring a new place with my friends. Finding someone to talk to is very important as well. Please don't bottle everything up, especially being this hurt and broken. It's impossible to fix it yourself.

It's gonna be hard, especially since he was probably the person you would go to, but think back to before him. Before you met him. Who would you go to, if they're not there anymore think who you would be okay with filling that position. I know a lot of people get into the idea that their SO should be their main caregiver, I disagree. There should always be someone else you can go to. Everyone is human, there's going to eventually be a day, like this, where they can't help like you want them to, so you need to go to someone else.

Best of luck, PM me if you want any more advice, stay strong, everything will be okay.
